solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sad as purr goes becoming affected scorn

indicators.note: sad here means in a sorry, wretched state, so the following words are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A melancholy cat's purr turns into a sneer of disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' looks like a mood for the purring cat but signals rearranging the letters of AS PURR GOES; 'becoming' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Aesop's fox, means pretending to despise something only because you cannot have it.

clue.text: Actor's fruit not finished? That is right

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the final letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: an olive is a small oily fruit
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: An actor wonders whether his fruit is unfinished and whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Actor stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most celebrated British stage and screen performers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Show signs of age in game on street

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the crossword's favourite game

explanation.surface: An old player showing his years during a game in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that corrodes over time is said to rust, and figuratively people or skills deteriorate with disuse.

clue.text: Forest worker phoned leading lady?

parts.note: to have phoned someone is to have rung them, past tense rang
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: Did the forester ring up the star actress?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a film star but means the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest ranger is employed to patrol and look after woodland and its wildlife.

clue.text: Formal request from favourite encountering opposition — not half!

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the word opposition is thrown away, keeping only its back half

explanation.surface: A formal appeal from a darling of the public who meets fierce resistance — and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads like the British exclamation meaning 'very much so', but it tells you to drop half of OPPOSITION, leaving ITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A petition is a written appeal, usually signed by many people, asking an authority to act.

clue.text: Obscure position of quiet cadet avoiding outsiders

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: avoiding outsiders means the outer letters of the word cadet are left off

explanation.surface: A quiet military cadet's hidden posting.
explanation.definitionFit: To shade something is to obscure it by blocking light from it, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Not to be used for personal cover?

definitions.text: Not to be used for personal cover?

parts.words: Not to be used for personal cover?
parts.note: sounds like an insurance exclusion, but means clothing too shabby or ill-fitting to put on

explanation.surface: A policy clause excluding something from personal insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests insurance; read it as clothes covering a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments unfit to be put on the body cannot serve as clothing, which is a person's covering.

clue.text: Opening for French teacher on way back with relative — a thrill

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of French is used
on the way back means the word for teacher is read in reverse

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: A French teacher drives home with a relative, feeling excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns SIR into RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement or emotion, a brief thrill.

clue.text: Ref had stay arranged for celebration

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee organised a break for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the June day when children honour their paternal parent with cards and gifts.

clue.text: Writer Mark's time alongside farm cart

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: An author's era spent beside a farm wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Mark stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist Samuel Clemens wrote under the pen name of Mark Twain.

clue.text: Neat extract from poet, Rimbaud

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tidy excerpt from the French poet Rimbaud.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim describes something tidy and well kept, much the same as neat.

clue.text: Poetry lover maybe ate these, cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and changed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover of verse perhaps eats these, once prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to beauty and the arts, of whom a poetry enthusiast is one example.

clue.text: Something disliked, marijuana the man's got inside

indicators.note: got inside says the letters sit within the words marijuana the man's

explanation.surface: An unpopular substance: marijuana that a man has smuggled in.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a thing or person intensely loathed, as in 'such ideas are anathema to him'.

clue.text: Little hesitation with tirade straying from standards

parts.note: er is the small sound of hesitating
a rant is a long angry tirade

explanation.surface: A slight pause and then an outburst from someone who has lapsed from good behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering from the proper course or from accepted standards of conduct.

clue.text: Agree Conservative needs to meet unpleasant guy

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, literally a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A Tory must meet a nasty man to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a formal synonym for agree.

clue.text: Charge to drink in Irish city — a good wine ultimately

parts.note: Cork is a city in the south of Ireland

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of wine is taken

explanation.surface: A fee for drinking a good wine in an Irish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Corkage is the fee a restaurant charges for serving wine the customer has brought.

clue.text: After play on words, is husband fine, say?

indicators.note: after means the later pieces follow the wordplay pun in the answer

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: After a joke, is the husband in good spirits?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as an adjective meaning well, but is the verb to impose a fine, an example of penalising.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing a monetary penalty is one way to discipline an offender.

clue.text: Boat sure to be damaged by him?

definitions.text: Boat sure to be damaged by him?

indicators.note: to be damaged means knocked out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A vessel certain to be wrecked by one particular wrecker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a wrecker is the one who would damage the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages property such as ships or machinery to obstruct an enemy.

clue.text: Seaside tree, by sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for the tree is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: the beech is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree growing by the coast, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore of sand or shingle at the edge of the sea, used here as a noun.

clue.text: On return, exclude a horse

indicators.note: on return means going back, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

explanation.surface: Coming back, a horse is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On return' turns BARA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian is a famous breed of fine-boned horse, often shortened in crosswords.

clue.text: Initially the operatives work near urban area

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: At first, the workers labour close to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up settlement larger than a village but smaller than a city.

clue.text: Knowing a type of pottery

parts.note: ware names a kind of ceramics, as in Delftware or stoneware

explanation.surface: Being expert about a particular style of ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious or informed of something, as in 'knowing the risks'.

clue.text: Wrath surrounding old scold for period

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for wrath goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ire is anger or wrath
to nag is to scold persistently

explanation.surface: Anger wrapping round an elderly nagging era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts ONAG inside IRE, after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era after the Bronze Age, when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: At work, he'd unearth recruitment agent

indicators.note: at work means busy operating on something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: On the job, he'd dig up the right staff for a recruiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A headhunter seeks out and approaches suitable candidates for senior jobs on behalf of firms.
